patient_script.opening_line: My right calf cramps up after I walk a couple of blocks, and I have to stop.
patient_script.behavior: Gruff, practical, thinks it is a pinched nerve like his brother had, impatient with questions about smoking.

if_asked.onset: Over about 8 months, slowly shorter walking distance
if_asked.pain quality: Tight, cramping ache in the right calf, 6 out of 10 when walking
if_asked.aggravating or relieving: Walking uphill is worse. Relief in 2 to 3 minutes standing still, no need to sit or bend forward
if_asked.neurologic: No back pain, no numbness, no weakness
if_asked.vascular: Right foot is often cold, a sore on the right big toe has not healed for 3 weeks

volunteers_only_if_asked: Toe sore not healing for 3 weeks
Pain happens with the same distance every time

exam_findings.vitals_and_general: Hypertensive, mildly overweight, brachial pressures slightly different
exam_findings.inspection: Right foot shiny, hairless skin, pale, 8 mm shallow ulcer on the right great toe tip with no drainage
exam_findings.palpation: Right foot cool to touch. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right, weak on the left. Femoral pulses present with a bruit on the right.
exam_findings.range_of_motion: Lumbar and hip motion full and painless, no pain reproduced
exam_findings.orthopedic_tests: SLR negative, Kemp negative, FABER negative. Straight standing extension of the lumbar spine does not reproduce the leg pain. Buerger test: pale on elevation, dusky red on lowering.
exam_findings.neurologic: Strength, reflexes and sensation normal, no cauda equina signs
exam_findings.other_system_exam: Heart regular, no murmur. Capillary refill 5 seconds right foot.

diagnosis.working: Peripheral arterial disease of the right leg with claudication and early critical limb ischemia
diagnosis.imaging_or_labs_to_order: Ankle brachial index, arterial duplex ultrasound, possibly CT angiography; lipid panel and A1c by medical doctor.
diagnosis.referral_or_emergency: Urgent vascular assessment within 24 to 48 hours because of the ulcer (same day if rest pain, color change or numbness); emergency room right away if the foot turns cold, blue or numb. No manipulation for leg pain.

model_soap.S: 66 year old male, 45 pack year smoker, high cholesterol. 8 months of right calf cramping at about two blocks, relieved by standing 2 to 3 minutes. Cold right foot. Toe sore for 3 weeks. No back pain or numbness.
model_soap.O: BP 158/92 right, 152/90 left. Right foot cool, shiny, hairless. 8 mm ulcer right great toe. Right DP and PT pulses absent, left weak. Right femoral bruit. Capillary refill 5 seconds. SLR, Kemp negative. Neuro intact. Buerger positive.
model_soap.A: Peripheral arterial disease with claudication and probable critical limb ischemia. Not neurogenic claudication, since standing relieves it and spine tests are negative.
model_soap.P: No manipulation. Urgent referral to vascular specialist within 48 hours for ABI and duplex. Sent note to his doctor. Do not walk on the ulcer, keep foot clean and dry. Stop smoking, resources given. ER now if foot turns blue, cold, numb or painful at rest.

common_errors: Calling it sciatica or a pinched nerve
Not checking pedal pulses
Missing the toe ulcer and cold foot
Failing to separate vascular from neurogenic claudication
Starting a walking program before a medical workup

title: Teen with a curve in her back

door_chart.vitals: BP 104/66, HR 72, RR 14, temp 98.2 F, height 5 ft 2 in (up 3 in this year), weight 108 lb
door_chart.chief_complaint: Mom noticed my shoulders look uneven
door_chart.history_on_chart: Mild ache between the shoulder blades after sports. No injury. Periods have not started yet.

patient_script.opening_line: My mom says one shoulder is higher, but I do not think it is a big deal.
patient_script.behavior: Shy, answers in short phrases, looks to her mother, a little self conscious about her body and dislikes being examined.

if_asked.onset: Mother noticed it 2 months ago, ache for a few weeks
if_asked.pain quality: Mild dull ache, 2 out of 10, after volleyball
if_asked.aggravating or relieving: Better with rest, no night pain
if_asked.family history: Her aunt wore a back brace as a teen
if_asked.growth: Grew 3 inches in a year, no period yet

volunteers_only_if_asked: She is embarrassed to change in the locker room

exam_findings.vitals_and_general: Healthy appearing teen, normal gait, no cafe au lait spots
exam_findings.inspection: Right shoulder higher, right scapula prominent, left waist crease asymmetry. Plumb line from C7 falls 1 cm to the right of the gluteal cleft.
exam_findings.palpation: Mild tenderness right thoracic paraspinals, no midline tenderness
exam_findings.range_of_motion: Full lumbar and thoracic motion, slight pain at end range right rotation
exam_findings.orthopedic_tests: Adams forward bend test: right rib hump of about 8 degrees on the scoliometer at T7. Leg lengths equal. SLR negative.
exam_findings.neurologic: Strength, sensation, reflexes normal. Abdominal reflexes symmetric. No clonus or Babinski.
exam_findings.other_system_exam: Skin without hairy patch or dimple over the spine, heart and lungs normal

diagnosis.working: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, right thoracic curve, skeletally immature
differential: Functional scoliosis from leg length difference
Osteoid osteoma or spinal tumor causing painful scoliosis
red_flags_to_catch: Pain at night or constant pain
diagnosis.imaging_or_labs_to_order: Standing PA full spine radiograph with Cobb angle and Risser sign, with shielding. MRI only if neurologic signs or atypical features appear.
diagnosis.referral_or_emergency: Referral to pediatric orthopedics because curve may be above 20 degrees in a premenarchal growing child. Not an emergency. Chiropractic exercise and monitoring only as shared care, no thrust to correct the curve.

model_soap.S: 13 year old female, premenarchal, grew 3 inches this year. Shoulder asymmetry noticed by mother 2 months ago. Mild thoracic ache after sports, 2 of 10, no night pain. No neuro symptoms. Aunt had scoliosis.
model_soap.O: Right shoulder and scapula high. Adams test: right thoracic rib hump, 8 degrees scoliometer. Leg lengths equal. No skin markers. Neuro and abdominal reflexes normal. SLR negative.
model_soap.A: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, right thoracic, skeletally immature. Differential: leg length cause, congenital curve, tumor. Right thoracic curve with pain this mild fits the usual pattern.
model_soap.P: Standing full spine radiographs with Cobb angle and Risser. Referral to pediatric orthopedics because she is still growing and the curve may need bracing. Measure again every 4 to 6 months. Core and posture exercises. No high velocity thrust. Return sooner for night pain, numbness or fast change. Parent given written plan. Mother and patient verbalized understanding and a chaperone was present throughout.

common_errors: Skipping the Adams forward bend test
Ignoring the growth stage and menstrual status
Promising a chiropractic adjustment will fix the curve
Missing the need to refer a growing child
Examining a minor without a chaperone or parent consent
